en.name: Andrew Kim Taegon
en.summary: The first native Korean Catholic priest, executed during the persecution of Christians in nineteenth-century Korea.
en.body: Andrew Kim Taegon was born into a Korean Catholic family at a time when Christianity was outlawed and practiced only in secret, and his own father was martyred for the faith when he was a boy. He traveled a grueling overland route to a seminary in Macau to train for the priesthood, one of the first Koreans ever to do so, and returned to his homeland by sea to be ordained secretly and begin ministering to the underground Church, working to establish routes by which foreign missionaries could enter the closed country. He was arrested while guiding missionaries across the border, tortured, and beheaded in 1846 at the age of twenty-five. He is honored, together with 102 other Korean martyrs including the laywoman Paul Chong Hasang, canonized as a group by Pope John Paul II in Seoul in 1984, the first canonization ceremony held outside Rome in modern times.
